Where it began

Cameron Bancroft was born in Attadale on 19 November 1992 and went to Aquinas College. He came up through Western Australia's under-17, under-19 and under-23 teams before moving on to the Australia Under-19 side, where he made three hundreds at an average of 50.90. At the 2012 Under-19 World Cup only one batsman scored more runs.

His senior career began on 16 October 2011, when he played a one-day game for Western Australia against Tasmania. His first-class debut followed a week later.

The player

He was first named in a Test squad in 2015, for a tour of Bangladesh that never went ahead, so the wait went on. His first cap for Australia came instead in a T20 international against India on 31 January 2016.

The Test debut finally arrived at home in the 2017–18 Ashes. Geoff Marsh presented him with his baggy green, and no Australian opener had made his Test debut in an Ashes match since Michael Slater in 1993. After 5 in the first innings he made 82 not out in the second as Australia won by ten wickets. In August 2019 he opened again in the Ashes, this time at Edgbaston. In 10 Tests between 2017 and 2019 he scored 446 runs at 26.24 with three fifties and a best of 82 not out, and took 16 catches.

What made him special

Bancroft was built for long days at the crease. In a Sheffield Shield match against New South Wales in February 2019 he made 138 not out and 86, facing 621 balls in all, just 28 short of Steve Waugh's record for a Shield game. He was the leading run-scorer in the 2022–23 Shield season with 945 runs at 59.06, and second the following summer with 778 at 48.62. That form put him among the leading names when Australia were looking for a new opener in early 2024.

He could get a move on too. On his one-day debut for Durham he hit 150 not out from 130 balls, and in the 2018–19 Big Bash he won a match award for the Perth Scorchers with 87 not out against the Sydney Sixers. A Test hundred was the one thing that got away. His unbeaten 82 on debut came closest.

Away from the middle

County cricket in England became a second home. Durham made him their captain for the 2019 season, and in February 2025 Gloucestershire named him captain of their red-ball side for that summer's County Championship. At home he played Big Bash cricket for the Perth Scorchers and later for the Sydney Thunder, alongside his first-class cricket for Western Australia.

And finally

Patience is half an opener's job, and Bancroft had plenty of practice. He was picked for a Test tour two years before he played a Test. His only T20 international went by without him facing a single ball, which at least left statisticians nothing to criticise. When the baggy green finally came, he was ready for it.
